text: # ZK60 decisions register — the rulings that govern the proof project
## At a glance
| D1 | Privacy scope: P1 hides inputs, outputs, activations (weights may be public); P3 also hides weights | **standing** | 2026-09-09 | Victor |
| D2 | Two lines: a zkVM intermediate delivers the first complete private tiny block; the custom-PCS line remains the route to the throughput target | **standing** | 2026-09-17 | Victor |
| D3 | Security level for the zkVM intermediate: about 97 bits conjectured soundness accepted, as a recorded deviation from the 128-bit target | **accepted** | 2026-09-18 | Victor |
| D4 | Groth16 trusted setup accepted for soundness of the zkVM intermediate's public artifact | **accepted** | 2026-09-18 | Victor |
| D5 | Public receipt kind: Groth16 only; composite never public; succinct is experimental evidence only | **decided (security review)** | 2026-09-18 | Fable disposition + Codex source review |
| D6 | Groth16 proving path on this box: native tools extracted from the official prover image, digests pinned (Docker absent) | **in progress** | 2026-09-18 | Codex (implementation) |

| D7 | New endpoint and weight identity profile for the zkVM route (salted SHA-256 commitments in a fixed journal; old PCS roots not compatible) | **accepted as the P1 statement of the zkVM line, with three recorded qualifiers**; the model approval record is still to be written | 2026-09-19 | Victor (Telegram 11:50); Codex implemented |

| D8 | Custom line, caller-fixed endpoint roots: obligation stands; the "two programmed points" closure is retracted for roots with any prior public opening | **corrected** | 2026-09-18 | Codex review; accepted by the security owner |

| D9 | Reduction-bias term of the prover's mask and pad draws on the custom line (about 2^-75 at the tiny shape, 2^-72 at 8B): accept as stated, or re-freeze fixtures with rejection sampling | **accepted as stated** | 2026-09-19 | Victor (Telegram 11:50) |

| D10 | Compact-PCS proof-size lever on the custom line (95–98 bits instead of 106) | **declined: keep the Ligero-class commitment** (the "free Merkle cap" first recorded beside this ruling is worth about 1% here, not 29% — corrected the same day) | 2026-09-19 | Victor (Telegram 11:50, phrased as a question and confirmed back to him) |

| D11 | D8's proposed reduction to empty history is not established by a consuming owner; prior authentication/hash history remains in scope | **technical correction** | 2026-09-18 | Codex native reproduction and independent review |

| D12 | Composed private block on the custom line: one proof, one transcript, two external endpoints; no commitment opened twice; hidden intermediates never get a shared caller-fixed endpoint; the second norm's int8 range proof is mandatory | **construction rule (restrictive; not a privacy acceptance)** | 2026-09-19 | Security owner (Fable), from the composition gap inventory |

| D13 | What the first MVP must prove: the hidden transformer blocks are enough; generating a token (embedding, final norm, head, token selection) is the next milestone | **decided** | 2026-09-19 | Victor (Telegram 11:50) |

| D14 | Commission a costed design memo for the fewer-hashed-bytes speed lever (encoding rate 1/2 and/or a 31–32-bit field). Paper only: building it would move every frozen digest and the soundness accounting, and stays a separate ruling | **memo commissioned** | 2026-09-19 | Victor (Telegram 11:50) |

| D15 | The custom line's "106 bits" is a per-opening figure; the projected whole 8B proof is about 94 bits. Every model-scale security statement quotes the whole-proof figure | **technical clarification**; the whole-proof target itself is a ruling still to be put to Victor | 2026-09-19 | Security owner (Fable), from `ZK60_FABLE_SECURITY_OBLIGATIONS.md` §5 and the D14 memo |

| D16 | Before the private block's norm is widened toward real-model widths, its denominator and the two isqrt witnesses keep a direct byte-limb range pin sized to the new maximum, at most four limbs each, with an exact remainder window | **construction rule (precondition for widening; soundness)** | 2026-09-19 | Security owner (Fable), from the norm range lane |

| D17 | Hiding endpoints beyond the tiny shape: the whole hidden plane is bound at every width (the batched multi-block seam, unconditional); the tiny private-IO path stays byte-frozen and new entry points are additive; a feed-forward-only private pass is a cost vehicle, never P1 | **construction rule (soundness) and a naming rule** | 2026-09-19 | Security owner (Fable), from the endpoints-at-scale draft and its independent check |

| D18 | Who fixes the commitment to a hidden input: **the prover, at proof time, for the first MVP** (what is built). A third party sealing an input in advance is a **recorded todo and the expected end state** — it needs a sealed handle that is not a polynomial-commitment root and a hashing gadget inside the proof (about +13% on the private pass [COUNTED, untested]; not built) | **decided: A now, B as a todo** | 2026-09-19 | Victor (Telegram 22:15) |

| D12a | Amendment to D12 for a private RUN of several blocks: a run is **one transcript end to end** with two external endpoints **for the run**, sealed by the prover (D18); each internal boundary plane is a hidden intermediate on **one prover-generated boundary commitment**, claimed by the two adjacent blocks, **one reserved pair per claim site, opened exactly once**, its row count **derived** as data + 2·sites + 2 (a single proximity row discloses 1 and the claim audit does not catch it); all five items of D12 carry over (no commitment opened twice; the second norm's int8 range proof holds at both ends of every boundary; **a boundary's scale is one field shared by both blocks, and the run absorbs one calibration identity**). Still forbidden: joining two finished runs (needs D18's option B **and** D8/D11 discharged); a boundary commitment fixed by anyone but the prover. Soundness of a twelve-block run at the 125M geometry about 2^-97.5 by the project's accounting — acceptance of that level is Victor's, pending | **construction rule (restrictive; not a privacy acceptance); paper only, nothing built** *[2026-09-23: "paper only, nothing built" is stale since the same day — the run was built on lane `zk60-private-block-125m` (stage 12) and measured: runs of 2, 3 and 12 blocks at the development rung verify from their segments; at the 125M shape a two-block run and a twelve-block run (484,100,736 B, 2026-09-20 11:22; dense witness after the S19-F1 repair 484,107,456 B, `m125-run-l12-dense.log`, 2026-09-20 21:01); the boundary geometry is derived in `boundary.rs` and any other

| D12b | Three construction rules for a private RUN, from the check of its composition argument. **(1) A run directory is publishable only if it contains the run statement, which is written only after the whole run has verified**; a directory without it is never transmitted and is removed by whoever launched the run; the refusal reason — which names the refusing stage, a function of the hidden input, because a run builds each block's witness inside its stage loop — is never shown to anyone not entitled to the input (rule M-9, an application of D21). "Admissible hidden input" is a joint condition on all stages. **(2) One randomness generator per run is accepted as built**, never cloned, forked or serialised, with the run's hidden input fixed before the first segment. **(3) Interior boundary scales are constants of the approved calibration**: a run refuses any other, so they are bound through the calibration identity it absorbs (before this they were bound by nothing; no proof byte moves) | **construction rules (restrictive; not a privacy acceptance)**; (3) to be built on the lane *[2026-09-23: (3) is built — lane stage 21 item 3 (`71c6509`, 2026-09-20 20:16): `RunStatement::new` refuses any interior scale pair other than the approved calibration's, failing-first recorded, and a test pins the run header's binding, boundary digests and parameter line byte-identical before and after (no absorb added, no proof byte moved). (1) is still a rule plus a test-only writer: `prove_run` has no production caller (ruling H-2; "the run layer is still dead code in release", lane stage 44).

| D19 | The hash functions are modelled as random oracles, in Fiat–Shamir and in the Merkle layer; the untagged shared BLAKE3 domain recorded as a deviation for the toy profile (challenges are 47-byte queries, a length nothing else uses; residual about 2^-241 — first written as 2^-243, corrected 2026-09-20 04:11 by an independent recount) and a separating tag added in new profiles | **ACCEPTED** | 2026-09-20 13:45 | Victor (console: "Yes on D19 D20 and D21"); one-pager `ZK60_RULINGS_FOR_VICTOR_PRIVACY.md` |

| D19a | How D19's tag is built, and one fixture outside it. **The tag is BLAKE3's keyed mode**: four public keys per profile (Fiat–Shamir transcript, column digest, salted Merkle leaf, Merkle inner node), each derived from the profile string; the verifier derives them from the profile it trusts, never from a receipt; a profile is either wholly on the legacy rule or wholly tagged, never a mixture. **In the model of D19 this reads the random oracle as a family of independent random functions indexed by BLAKE3's mode and key** (distinct profiles share a key only with negligible probability). Tagged: the generalised development rung, the 125M block, the multi-block run (a run uses its shape's keys and is separated from a single-block proof by its own domain string, absorbed first under the transcript key). **Built and reviewed 2026-09-20 15:50** (lane `zk60-private-block-125m` at `9ded619`; additions only in the shared files but for four transcript lines that are the identical call under the legacy rule). Never tagged: the toy (frozen; D22 rests on its bytes). **Outside the obligation, by name: the frozen-seam development rung** — its endpoint is committed inside a frozen file, so it keeps the legacy rule as a whole; it is a stepping-stone fixture, never a deliverable, and **may not appear in any privacy statement**. A tagged commitment declines the GPU hasher until a keyed device path exists — a temporary CPU fallback, not a performance result | **construction ruling under D19 (not a privacy acceptance)** | 2026-09-20 15:01 | Security owner (Fable), after the integrator's rev

| D19b | **The model behind the tag of D19a — proposed, for Victor.** D19a reads D19's random oracle as a family of independent random functions, one per BLAKE3 mode **and key**. Corrections to D19a's own text (2026-09-21 01:12): that is **not** "BLAKE3's own design claim" — the designers' claim separates the three *modes*, whereas the salted-leaf and inner-node functions are the *same* mode under different **published** keys; and the randomness generator is **not** keyed (only its key derivation is; its stream is unkeyed BLAKE3 over key and counter). The honest model is that **BLAKE3's compression function is ideal, also when the adversary knows and chooses the chaining value it starts from** — the assumption under which BLAKE3 is shown to behave as a random function at all, but stronger than D19 as it was put to Victor. Nothing accepted rests on it (no tagged profile has a privacy statement; D22 is the untagged toy), and nothing measurable changes: the tag removes two terms of about 2^-241 and 2^-485 and adds a key-collision term of about 2^-251, zero for the keys that exist, by test. Recorded alternative: a one-byte prefix per domain under the single unkeyed function — inside D19 exactly, about half a percent of hashing, and a redo of the tag stage | **ACCEPTED by Victor 2026-10-17 19:28 UTC** ("all recommendations yes", in the Claude console, answering the sheet `ZK60_RULINGS_FOR_VICTOR_20261017.md`; the same answer came by Telegram at 19:24); proposed text unchanged | 2026-09-21 01:12 | Security owner (Fable), from the independent check of the run's hash-layer argument

| D20 | Timing, memory and power are out of scope for the first MVP; **refusals are NOT** — they stay inside the privacy argument (challenge-only, about 2^-62; one of eighteen classes is input-dependent at about 2^-112 and is carried as a named residual) | **ACCEPTED** | 2026-09-20 13:45 | Victor (console); same one-pager |

| D21 | Rejected receipts are never transmitted, and retained capture bundles count as publishing: nothing computed from a hidden input may be added to them; a refusal reason is never shown to anyone not entitled to the input | **ACCEPTED** | 2026-09-20 13:45 | Victor (console); same one-pager |

| D22 | **Privacy accepted for ONE artifact: the toy private-block profile `hashline-zk-mr1/private-block-t32-poc/1`** (one block, 32 tokens, width 16, public synthetic weights, the prover sealing its own endpoints per D18): in the random-oracle model (D19), under the named generator assumption, an accepted receipt's view is within about 2^-77.7 per proof of one that does not depend on the hidden input, output or activations; refusal is challenge-only up to 2^-112; timing, memory and power out of scope (D20); operating rules of D21. **It is an argument each of whose steps survived one independent attack, not a proof re-derived by the security owner; it lapses for any code that changes one of its seven conditions. It covers NOTHING else: not the development rung, not the 125M block, not any multi-block run, not real weights, not sealing in advance (D8 and D11 untouched), not soundness**. *Scope said more exactly on 2026-09-21 03:23: it covers the profile on the **CPU path** — at this untagged profile a GPU-feature build with the accelerator enabled hashes columns with two hand-written CUDA kernels and moves blinding material to device memory, and that configuration is not covered until it has been read; and "the generator" means the proof's three generators jointly, separate operating-system entropy reads being assumed independent. On 2026-09-20 22:06 it was re-read against the integrator's merged code (`4751b93`) and its source pins extended to all 29 files on its path. On 2026-09-21 10:44 the refusal clause was sharpened, number unchanged (statement §9 item 10; ruling V-3

| D23 | **An accepted receipt's endpoint roots are never registered, republished or referred to by a later artifact — proposed, for Victor.** The privacy case's hypothesis O-2 / ask R-9 (`ZK60_PRIVACY_CASE_FIRST_MVP.md` §1.2 item 1, §5.2, l.1633, l.1801): the moment a later artifact refers to an accepted receipt's two endpoint roots (e.g. chains its output root into another proof, or records it in a registry), the D8/D11 question applies and D22 no longer covers that receipt. It was never put to Victor nor listed in D22's statement; found 2026-09-23 by `ZK60_BLINDING_LAW_GR4_TOY_READING.md`. The security owner carries it as a stated hypothesis of the toy statement (§6) from 2026-09-23 16:52; the argument and its figures are unchanged. Constrains operations, so it is Victor's | **ACCEPTED by Victor 2026-10-17 19:28 UTC** ("all recommendations yes", in the Claude console, answering the sheet `ZK60_RULINGS_FOR_VICTOR_20261017.md`; the same answer came by Telegram at 19:24); proposed text unchanged | 2026-09-23 16:52 | Security owner (Opus 5.5 session continuing the Fable lane); one-pager `ZK60_RULINGS_FOR_VICTOR_PRIVACY.md` |

| D24 | **Norm precision per profile instead of a fifth remainder limb — proposed 2026-10-17.** New trained profiles lower `NORM_TN` (10 at width 2048, 9 at width 4096) and scale the norm multiplier with it, so the exact remainder window stays at most 32 bits (four byte limbs, D16 rule 4); `D_max` for new profiles counts int16 -32768 and the profile's epsilon; old profiles stay byte-frozen | **ACCEPTED 2026-10-17 (security-owner lane, after two independent review rounds): norm rule, per-profile shifts, trained profile and loader; conditions R2-a/R2-b being fixed; round 3 (18:36 UTC) accepted the Llama-3-8B profile changes on soundness, verifier-DoS finding r3_6 open; not a privacy acceptance** | 2026-10-17 | Claude (security-owner lane) |

| D25 | **Proving the next token (D13's next milestone): eight product rulings T1–T8.** T1 one hidden next token per run first (mode i), a whole greedy continuation in one pass later (mode ii); T2 the prompt length stays hidden in mode (i) and is sealed inside the input endpoint so the owner can check it (needs the security-owner ruling R9 on the two-site endpoint geometry); T3 ties go to the lowest token id (numpy first maximum); T4 (amended 2026-10-17 20:21 UTC, option (b)) the integer head uses per-row int8 scales with 12-bit integer multipliers, and is accepted if its token equals the float head's on the same stack output at every held-out position where the float head's top-2 margin is >= 0.3 logits (measured 100%; overall 98.9%; every miss a float near-tie) — the original >= 99% overall threshold was missed (98.45% per-tensor, 98.91% per-row; `results/zk60_token_io_fidelity_20261017/REPORT.md`) and the 16-bit final-norm alternative (99.57%) was declined; T5 the verifier never sees the token: the prover hands the owner the token and the endpoint opening privately and the owner checks it against the receipt (rests on D21 and D23); T6 repeated one-token runs are not a proved token stream and every claim says so; T7 the receipt names the embedding and head by export digest, not proved to come from the checkpoint (as for the blocks under D24); T8 the proof forces the BOS token at position 0. Design `results/zk60_token_io_design_20261017/DESIGN.md`, adversarial check `.../check/CHECK.md` (core sound; binding changes B-1..B-3 folded in before rung R1) | **ACCEPTED by Victor

| D26 | **The two-site input token endpoint (R9; token-I/O run profiles only).** For a token-I/O run that hides the prompt length (D25 T2) or proves a greedy continuation (mode ii), the external input token endpoint is a hiding commitment with **two claim sites**: derived geometry `rows = data + 2·2 + 2`, row width 2^8, rate 1/8 (2^-106.25 per opening), its own spec type and digest domain, any other row count refused by name; prover-sealed (D18), root never referred to later (D23); claimed exactly twice — stage IN's IO-in on half 0 (public half bit 0) and stage OUT's IO-s on half 1 (`s = e_{P−1}`; SHIFT in mode ii) at public half bit 1 — each with its own reserved pair and each IO slot over its whole half with the public support factor; **opened exactly once after stage OUT and `B_out`**, the verifier refusing any other place, claim count or second opening; variant (public row / P / F), geometry and opening place fixed by the run statement, never by a segment; the owner re-encodes at the derived geometry and checks the root, the profile's BOS, the prompt, pad ids, zero pad words and `s = e_{P−1}`. **Variant P adopted; F (selector in the output endpoint) the recorded fallback; C not adopted.** Conditions C-a..C-e of the second check bind. Design fixes N-1 (the BOS clause gets its own fresh challenge drawn after `A_in`), N-2 (BOS id a per-profile statement constant in [0, V)) and N-3 (every batched clause has a fresh challenge) are part of building to this rule | **construction rule (security owner); not a privacy acceptance** — the D17 rule-3 joint-view gate (G-6/G-7) on cap

| D27 | **The custom line's soundness target (question G.0-2).** The target is stated **per run at a named workload** (today Llama-3-8B, T = 512) as a whole-run union bound, with the forger-work-per-attempt reading quoted beside it. **MVP: about 95 bits whole-run (derived lookup bound, D15 note of 20:10; about 99.7 bits as work per attempt) is accepted as a recorded deviation**, next to the zkVM line's 97 conjectured (D3); **next milestone: 100 bits whole-run**, preferably through LogUp-GKR with a 256-bit lookup challenge (otherwise lookup repetition at about −33% throughput); **product: 128**. Throughput is not traded for bits at the MVP; near-free levers (more column checks) may be taken when convenient. Victor's reasoning: throughput matters more for applications than making the protocol "ridiculously unbeatable"; at about 95 bits a forgery needs about a million A100s for about 8,700 years or the whole Bitcoin network for about a year (generous one-hash-per-try estimate) | **ACCEPTED by Victor 2026-10-17 20:21 UTC** ("G.0-2 yes", Claude console); memo `results/zk60_soundness_recount_20261017/MEMO_G02.md`, lookup-bound check `.../check_logup/CHECK.md`; every security statement quotes the whole-run figure with its workload. **Direction added by Victor 20:22 UTC: proofs must eventually be selectable at different security standards for more critical applications.** Consequences: the security tier (e.g. MVP ~95, 100, 128 whole-run at the named workload) is a profile parameter bound into the run statement, with its derived whole-run figure; the verifier takes a minimum tier as

| D28 | **CS-2 and CS-5 are not needed at the trained profiles.** The 125M lane's refusal rulings CS-2 and CS-5 guard against shapes whose arithmetic windows could be set loosely; at the trained profiles every window is derived and checked exactly at construction (`shape.rs` ~1196-1200, ~1238-1246; `layout.rs` ~1080-1082) and the width is capped at 4096, so neither ruling adds a refusal the trained door does not already make. The trained privacy statement records them as unnecessary on these code facts | **construction reading (security owner); not a privacy acceptance** — reopen if a trained profile ever admits a declared (not derived) window or a width above 4096 | 2026-10-19 09:31 | Claude (coordinating session as security owner), on the privacy review (`results/zk60_privacy_review_trained_t32_20261017/REVIEW.md` P-13, `REVIEW2.md`) and the native tree |

| D29 | **The refusal census is a completeness item, not a condition of the trained privacy statement.** Since native R6 the honest prover runs the CS-3 lookup-miss refusal on every sealed witness in the sealing pass, before the run header exists (review r6, N-r5-a), so every refusal the trained door or the witness builder can make happens before anything is published (H-1 by code). Under D20/D21 a refused input publishes nothing; how often honest inputs are refused (GN-1/GS-14) is therefore a completeness and usability measurement, still owed, but it no longer bounds the privacy sentence | **reading (security owner); not a privacy acceptance** — reopen if any refusal can occur after the run header | 2026-10-19 09:31 | Claude (coordinating session as security owner), on `REVIEW2.md` Q-7 and `results/zk60_d24_review_20261017/R6_VERDICT.md` |

| D30 | **DD, the per-row division dictionary, admitted into the Llama-3-8B T512 profile specification.** Each attention row gets `cap` committed slots (key = row id or row Sum, public e from sorted({0} ∪ exp outputs), P_dict = floor(e·2^F_P/Sum) proved by the existing exact-division relation with byte-limb windows); each score entry does one tuple lookup into its row's slots instead of carrying its own division limbs. Bit-exact; −20.8% committed elements, −28.2% byte lookups, −20.1% zero-check work at 8B T512 [COUNTED]; supersedes EXR; FN stays a fallback. Conditions (binding): (1) every dictionary position is a valid tuple — division clauses and limb lookups at every slot of a true row with no usage gate, pads (key, 0, 0) and pad-zero limbs, multiplicities and helpers never gated; (2) tuples and multiplicities committed in `A` before β, γ, α, a distinct tag and β² for P; (3) the table helper in the single value-0 sum claim with sign −1, every dictionary plane opened only at its own reserved site, no virtual claim, P-3 unchanged; (4) the prover inverts every dictionary slot on every attempt, and the refusal residual 2·L·(768 + rows·cap)/p² (~2^-103 per 32-block run) replaces D22 §9 item 10's challenge-only sentence for this profile; (5) lookup term (N + 2303 + 4·rows·cap)/|F| per block, P's range accepted as range-by-membership in D16 rule 5's audit; (6) a profile whose exp tables need more than `cap` slots is refused at the trained door by name before any header; plus binding changes B-1..B-8 of the check | **construction rule (security owner); paper only, nothing built;

| D31 | **pg_rot1's identical lookup pairs are kept, as read; the declared class is not restricted.** At the trained TinyLlama export pg_rot1 four lookup pairs coincide (F RGL, Q RQL, Kv RKL, RVL), each landing in one paired LogUp helper whose relation has two equal denominators (H[19], H[26], H[28], H[39]). G-7 read them at the trained export: no duplicated H plane, no repeated terminal coordinate, no two equal published values in any capture; NL-1 S0–S5 pass; terminal surjection A 36/36 disclosed 0, H 8/9 with the LogUp sum claim disclosing exactly the declared 2, endpoints and boundary 0. Soundness of a paired helper with equal members is the LogUp check's counted case. Restricting the class to sh <= 7 (no such pairs) would discard the evidence of record for no measured gain | **reading (security owner); not a privacy acceptance** — reopen if a capture ever shows a duplicated plane, a repeated terminal coordinate or equal published values from these pairs | 2026-10-19 10:29 | Claude (coordinating session as security owner), on the gate's G-7 (`results/zk60_gate_tinyllama_20261017/g7/`) |

| D32 | **Fidelity target: no performance degradation versus the float model.** The proved integer model must score essentially the same as the original float model on task performance (held-out perplexity and downstream benchmarks); token-by-token agreement with the float model is a diagnostic, not the target. Today's gap: held-out perplexity 9.72 -> 15.48 at Llama-3-8B T128 (export b7) and 12.67 -> 15.80 at TinyLlama-1.1B T128; the exact metric set and the numeric "no degradation" threshold are proposed by the fidelity lane for Victor to confirm. Weight-side calibration (rounding, scale folding, rotations, calibration data) costs the proof nothing because weights are public and fixed; profile changes are costed against the speed plan | **ACCEPTED by Victor 2026-10-19 11:30 UTC** (Claude console: "fidelity target: no performance degredation versus float"; also stated by Telegram at 11:28 UTC). **Threshold RULED by Victor 2026-10-19 ~17:00 UTC** (Claude console: "fidelity target: ppl <= 1.01, LAMBADA >= 99%, no refusals"): held-out perplexity of the integer model at most **1.01x** the float model's (on the fidelity lane's held-out sets, FineWeb and WikiText); LAMBADA accuracy at least **99%** of the float model's; **zero** refusals on the evaluation sets. The threshold is on the point estimates; confidence intervals are reported beside them (the proposal's extra "upper CI <= 1.02" clause was not part of the ruling). **Threshold AMENDED by Victor 2026-10-21 ~00:19 UTC** (Claude console: "As far as fidelity goes, 1-2% is acceptable so I'd say let's fix the refusals and procee

| D33 | **Privacy accepted for ONE artifact: an accepted, bound run of the trained TinyLlama-1.1B T32 profile** (`hashline-zk-mr1/private-run-tinyllama-1.1b-t32-trained-statement/1`, calibration `pg_rot1_export_T32` profile.json `b25ba5f5…`, L = 1, 2 and 22, the CPU binary `e51cc6a4…` built from native R7 tree `36a8aed1…` with its 46 pins): in the random-oracle model for BLAKE3 read per D19b, under the generator assumption E-1 / X-1, an accepted run's view is within about **2^-74.8 / 2^-73.8 / 2^-70.4** per run (L = 1 / 2 / 22) of one that does not depend on the hidden run input, output, activations or internal boundary planes, for every admissible input; the refusal fact is challenge-only up to 2^-117.4 / 2^-116.4 / 2^-113.0. In plain words: someone checking a proof of the 22-layer TinyLlama stack learns nothing about the hidden prompt, activations or output, except with odds around one in 2^70 per run (about one in 2^40 over a billion runs). **Not covered:** other calibrations (dg, b4, every per-layer export), other T, the GPU path, the next-token stages (embedding / final norm / head / token choice; gate round 7 owed), Llama-3-8B, soundness (the D24 review's), the refusal fact itself. Like D22 it is an argument whose steps survived one independent attack per step (three review rounds), not a proof re-derived by the security owner | **ACCEPTED by Victor 2026-10-19 16:56 UTC** (Claude console: "accept thrTinyLlama privacy statement"), on the coordinating session's recommendation; **IN FORCE for R7 only** — native R8 changes five pinned files (`private_block.rs`, `run.rs`,

| D34 | **Next-token stages: the input-dependent LogUp refusal is priced as a distance term, as D30 (4) did for DD.** In the next-token profiles (public-row variant) stage IN inverts only the prompt's own τ rows (at most T distinct, q_t = τ(tok_t), no position tag) and stage OUT at most 256 byte values; nothing is drawn or absorbed in between, the message is constant and there is no retry. Whether the prover hits a zero denominator there therefore depends on hidden data. Accepted as a counted two-world distance of 2·(768L + 32 + 256)/p² per run (2^-116.96 at L = 1 by this formula, the figure the statement carries; the reviewer's tight count is about 2^-117.14 — wording corrected 2026-10-20 04:33 UTC on the gate's note), which replaces, for the token stages, the "refusal is a function of the challenges and public tables alone" sentence; any next-token privacy statement must carry it.
